premises.text: People often stick to familiar places instead of trying new ones due to uncertainty about the experience.
premises.evidence_span: we don't want to take the chance and try to go to a new place, because we're not sure that we're going to like the experience.

premises.text: SpotOn uses social network data to provide personalized recommendations.
premises.evidence_span: SpotOn cuts through the noise by pulling in your existing social network data from Facebook and Foursquare, and uses it to build a profile of you to give you personalized and actionable recommendations.

premises.text: Recommendations are based on friends' ratings rather than random reviews.
premises.evidence_span: These are my friends. These are not random people. These are not Yelp reviewers that I don't care about.

premises.text: Users can contribute preference data to improve recommendations for themselves and others.
premises.evidence_span: Every piece of data that I contribute to Spot On adds to this entirely new layer of information that did not exist before.

premises.text: SpotOn provides a personalized search experience based on user preferences and friends' activities.
premises.evidence_span: we present this all to you in a very simple but powerful way in a final search view.

premises.text: SpotOn aims to enhance the social experience of going out with friends.
premises.evidence_span: Spot On is not about the recommendation. It is about the end experience of being at that bar with your friends and having a good time.

value.text: Users enjoy a more fulfilling social experience by discovering new places with friends.
value.evidence_span: we want you to actually find a place so you're enjoying, spend more time actually enjoying the place with your friends.

notes: No separate premises for features like PixView or filters as they support the same core premise of personalized recommendations.
